title: NudgePaid event reports balance snapshot, not actual delivered amount, for fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens
description: `nudgeAmount` is computed as `balanceOf(address(this))` and then both transferred and emitted in the event. For fee-on-transfer or rebasing ERC20 tokens, the recipient receives less than `nudgeAmount` while the event records the pre-transfer snapshot. Off-chain consumers (yield funnel reconciliation, dashboards, accounting) reading `NudgePaid.amount` will overstate the delivered amount.
exploit_scenario: Owner sets `nudgePaymentToken` to a token with a 1% transfer fee. Contract holds 100 tokens, calls `safeTransfer(recipient, 100)`. Recipient receives 99. Event emits `NudgePaid(recipient, token, 100)`. Off-chain accounting believes 100 was paid out; reconciliation against the recipient's balance shows a 1-token discrepancy.
recommended_mitigation: Either (a) document that nudge token must not be FoT/rebasing, (b) snapshot recipient balance before and after the transfer and emit the delta, or (c) snapshot this contract's balance before and after and emit the difference. Option (c) is cheapest.
notes: Pure accounting / event hygiene issue. Per project's known-invalid list, fee-on-transfer tokens are typically out of scope unless explicitly supported, but the rebasing-token side may still apply; demoted to low/QA.
